body:
Follow-up to #7925. That issue listed "unconfirmed candidates" for tests that cannot fail and stopped there. This issue records the result of mutation-testing every one of them.

## The class

Tests that cannot fail: the assertion is skipped, vacuous, or satisfied by a constant, so the code the test names can be broken without the test noticing.

## Charter

The unconfirmed candidates of #7925, and nothing else. Method per site: decide what the test claims to protect, break that code with a marker proving the broken line ran, and see whether the test stays green. Real means it stays green. Not real means a named assertion fails. Sites in files touched by an open pull request, and the five sites already fixed in #7927, were left alone. No production code changed. This issue ends when every candidate in #7925 is either fixed here or ruled out below.

## Confirmed (the break the test missed, and the fix)

| Site | The break that stayed green | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/cli/src/commands/gym.test.ts` (`totalClashes >= 0`) | the clash channel forces its total to 0 (score becomes 1, still self-consistent) | new seeded-episode test requires a positive count and a score below 1 |
| `packages/mcp/test/integration.test.ts` (`model_audit` range) | `overall` forced to 0 | assert identity is 100, no duplicate GlobalIds, and `overall` is the rounded mean of the three category scores |
| `packages/provenance/test/merge-battery.test.ts` (`falseConflictRate` range) | `falseConflictRate` forced to 0 (12 runs all green) | recompute the rate from its counts, require false conflicts to occur, and check `killCriterionPass` against it |
| `packages/clash/src/contact/min-distance.test.ts` (triangle indices `>= 0`) | both indices forced to 0, only one forced to 0, or the two swapped | require each named triangle to contain its witness point, with each mesh being the large one once so the index is unambiguous |
| `packages/lists/src/engine.zone.test.ts` (3 places) and `engine.geometry.test.ts` (1 place) | the engine returns no rows: `rows.every(...)` is true over nothing | assert the expected row count first |
| `rust/export/src/rebar_fabrication_tests.rs` (2 places) | the precheck drops every requested check for a modified or unsupported source: `all(Uncheckable)` is true over an empty list | assert the sweeps exist and every requested check kind is reported |
| `packages/collab/test/color.test.ts` (same-expression determinism) | the FNV-1a offset basis or prime changed: the whole collab suite (306 tests) stayed green, although the module promises the same color for the same id across machines | pin `fnv1a` to the published 32-bit reference vectors |

## Ruled out (the assertion that caught the break)

| Site | Break | Caught by |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/server-client/src/geometry-diagnostics-contract.test.ts` (`expect(true)` after `expectTypeOf`) | a field added to the wire copy of `GeometryDiagnostics` | `pnpm typecheck` fails with TS2344 on the `toEqualTypeOf` line, so the type assertion bites; the runtime placeholder is harmless |
| `rust/export/src/gltf_conformance_tests.rs` and `gltf_tests.rs` (13 `if let Some` sites) | instrumented first: every one of the 13 branches is entered on the fixtures (2 to 3404 times each). Then 13 exporter breaks: byte stride off by 2 (flat and batch paths), stride dropped (both paths), accessor `min` off by 1, normal accessor count plus 1, material index out of range, node mesh index out of range, nodes with no mesh, empty `GlobalId`, `modelId` leaked when none was given, root children dropped, instance matrix translated | `*_export_is_structurally_conformant`, `quantized_glb_is_structurally_valid`, `nodes_carry_global_id_and_model_id`, `instanced_occurrences_reconstruct_world_positions` and others (1 to 13 failing tests per break). The one `matrix` length check cannot fail by construction because the field is `[f32; 16]` |
| `packages/diff/src/fingerprint.test.ts` | random noise added to `stableHash` | "is deterministic and distinguishes inputs" and the FNV vector test |
| `packages/lens/src/colors.test.ts` | random noise added to `uniqueColor` | "is deterministic" and "pins the exact hex output" |
| `packages/extensions/src/authoring/prompt.test.ts` | random text prepended to the contract | "is deterministic, same string across calls" |
| `rust/export/src/usd/tests.rs` (two places) | a call counter appended to the USDA output | `deterministic` and `instancing_deterministic` |

For the determinism sites the claim is determinism, and each test does catch a break of that claim. Only the collab site also lacked a pinned value; the others have one (diff, lens) or assert structure that a changed value would not preserve. The prompt and USD sites were not tested for a deterministic-but-wrong value.

## Observation, not diagnosed

While strengthening the gym test I found that `AB22.ifc` currently produces 0 clashes through the gym clash channel (18 elements, all `IfcPavement`, `IfcCourse` or `IfcEarthworksFill`), and `ifc-lite clash AB22.ifc` also reports 0. The comment above `AB22_TIMEOUT_MS` in the same test file says the count went from 19 to 75 after #1910 and that ten `IfcFacilityPart` solids are now meshed. Neither matches what I measured on current `main`. I did not bisect it, so I cannot say whether the comment is stale or something regressed. That is why the new gym test uses a seeded episode instead of pinning AB22.

comments.body: Fix branch pushed: `audit/vacuous-tests-2` (head b8407fe6ce2d34945522a4ac49cf663483f5e3cd), based on current `main`, one commit per site, test-only changes, no pull request until this is labelled `ready`. Each strengthened test fails under the break listed above and passes without it. The cli and mcp suites have failures in the BCF publication tests, none of which this branch touches (not compared against a clean `main` run); the `export_golden` integration tests could not run here because a landxml fixture was absent.

Finding for the `gym.test.ts` clash-channel site: the AB22.ifc count of 0 is not a regression. It is the end of two deliberate changes, and the comment in the test ("clash count 19 -> 75") has been stale since the first one.

How the 0 arises on current `main` (779a431a28): the model is found and meshed, the default self-clash rule (`a: '*'`, hard) matches 18 elements and examines 50 candidate pairs, and none of them crosses. `ifc-lite clash tests/models/AB22.ifc --json` reports `total: 0` with `ruleCoverageOutcome: "clean"`, so this is a real "ran and found nothing", not an empty input or a missing file. The gym clash channel builds the same elements and the same single rule through the same engine.

Measured history (same command, wasm and TS rebuilt at each commit, bisected on `upstream/main`):

| Count | At | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 75 | af869bd6c8 (#1970) | the ten IfcFacilityPart road-surface solids are meshed |
| 19 | 081ed7e7e3 (#2572) | spatial containers are no longer clash bodies, so those ten solids drop out of the clash set again. The 75 was only ever true between #1970 and #2572 |
| 7 | 4d19160676 | the 19 coplanar layer contacts reduce to 7 (intermediate step, not bisected further) |
| 0 | 0576221cbd (#5564) | tri-tri contact within f32 noise is now touch, independent of the origin (#5406). The first commit at which the count is 0; its parent gives 7 |

At the parent of #5564 the 7 hits are all IfcCourse/IfcPavement layers with `distanceKind: estimate` (AABB estimates of 0.3 m to 2.7 m for layers whose boxes overlap). #5564 changes the SAT to treat overlap inside a per-axis f32 noise band as separation, and its message records the intended effect on a comparable infra case ("Infra-Bridge CLI-default count 50 -> 2 hard"). I did not independently prove that each of the 7 is a flush contact rather than a true overlap, so that part rests on the commit's own pinned tests.

Consequence for #7928: a positive-count assertion on AB22 will fail on `main`, so the fixture cannot carry the "clash count must be positive" check. Either seed an in-process model with a known overlap (the `--seed` factory already generates models in-process and always runs) or pick a fixture with a known positive count, and replace the "19 -> 75" sentence in the comment, which is true of no commit on `main` today.
